Subject: Logs - retention windows, exports & delete attestations

Hi Diego,

We're preparing for an upcoming SAR and I need to confirm a few things about Acme's tenant logs on Redwood:

- What are the default retention windows for access logs vs audit (admin) logs for EU tenants?
- Can we request a per-tenant export (slice) that contains only the activity for a custom date range? What formats do you provide for exports (NDJSON, Parquet, CSV, etc)?
- Do export packages include hashes/manifests we can use as proof of export and integrity?
- If we request deletion of retained logs (e.g., to complete a DSAR or a legal hold release), what proof/certification does Redwood provide that the data was deleted? Is there an attestation template you can share?
- Finally: do logs contain PII (full IPs, usernames) or are there configurable redaction/pseudonymization options?

We need answers by early next week — can you loop in whoever from Redwood handles export SLAs and legal attestations?

Thanks,
Anita Singh
Head of Security Operations

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Anita Singh <anita.singh@acmeretail.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 16:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Logs - retention windows, exports & delete attestations

Hi Anita — thanks for the clear checklist. Short answers below and I'll loop in Kimberly (privacy/legal) and Marissa (customer ops) for the formal artifacts and SLA confirmation.

- Default windows (EU tenants): access/event logs: 90 days; audit/admin logs: 2 years (enterprise tier). Both can be customized per contract.
- Exports: we support per-tenant, per-date-range exports. Standard delivery formats: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON) and compressed Parquet (recommended for large ranges). We can also provide CSV on request for small slices.
- Integrity: export packages include a manifest (file list + SHA256 checksums) and a timestamped signed manifest (PDF) for chain-of-custody.
- Deletion proof: we provide a deletion attestation that includes the tenant id, affected ranges, export manifest id (if an export was produced), and a signed statement that stored copies were removed from our primary stores and backups in accordance with the contract. The attestation includes timestamps and the operator id.
- PII: logs may contain identifiers (obfuscated user ids, truncated IP by default). We offer redaction/pseudonymization options: masking IP octets, hashing user identifiers, or suppressing user identifiers entirely for exported slices. Note: retrospective redaction of already-exported artifacts is not possible — we can only redact at export time or delete storage copies.

Next steps: Kimberly will share the attestation template and the standard SLA timeframe for ad-hoc exports (we typically aim for 5 business days, 48 hours for expedited enterprise requests). Marissa will follow up with the checklist to collect tenant id, date ranges, and delivery preferences.

I'm attaching the internal export checklist and the current attestation template as a starting point (see attached).

Thanks — Diego

Thanks Diego. Quick legal/ops clarifications for Acme:

- Attestation: the attached attestation_template.pdf (v2) is our standard. It includes tenant id, export manifest checksum, operator id, deletion timestamps, and a statement of procedure. For customer-facing attestation we stamp and sign from Redwood Legal. If Acme requires a custom statement we can add contract language but that typically requires an amendment.
- SLA / timelines: standard ad-hoc export is 5 business days for a <90-day slice; for larger ranges (multi-months or years) expect 7-10 business days depending on size and retention tier. Expedited handling (48–72 hours) is available under Enterprise support and will incur an expedite fee unless otherwise contracted.
- Delivery & residency: EU-region exports can be delivered to an EU destination (e.g., S3 eu-west-1) via pre-signed URL or direct transfer. The manifest will contain the delivery URL and the SHA256s. For customers with data residency clauses we can generate region-bound slices only; cross-border slices require an approved export authorization form.
- PII & redaction: by default logs are pseudonymized: usernames are stored as internal IDs; IPs are stored with last octet truncated. For exports we can apply additional masks or hash values. Important: once an export is provided to the customer, Redwood cannot retract or modify that exported file — so recommend redaction at export time if PII is a concern.
- Deletion attestation process: operations will run the erase workflow (primary store deletion + verified tombstone of backup partitions) and produce a signed attestation referencing the export manifest id (if applicable), the archival ids removed, and the operator runbook version. We also produce a manifest of removed object ids and a proof-of-deletion timestamp (system-generated).

Action items for Diego / Marissa:
- Diego: confirm Acme tenant id and exact date ranges they want exported.
- Marissa: prepare the order in our export queue, mark expedite if Acme requests and confirm cost.
- I (Kimberly): will sign and return the attestation template once you provide the final manifest id and deletion range.
